items.summary: Times Higher Education (THE) is considering halving the weight of citation impact in its 2028 World University Rankings, a move that could benefit Korean universities struggling in the indicator. Under the proposed changes, four indicators measuring research quality — citation impact, research strength, research excellence and research influence — would each account for 7.5 percent of a university's overall score. The proposal would halve citation impact's current weighting of 15 percent while raising the other three indicators from 5 percent to 7.5 percent each, keeping the overall weight of research quality unchanged at 30 percent. Puden Tsang, THE's regional director for Japan, Malaysia, South Korea and Thailand, outlined the proposal Wednesday during a data masterclass at the THE Innovation & Impact Summit 2026. The changes have yet to be finalized, with THE seeking feedback from universities and conducting further testing before confirming its 2028 methodology. The Seoul Central District Court delivered the verdict in the case against Choo, who stood trial on charges of playing a key role in Yoon's alleged insurrection. Choo was accused of changing the venue of an emergency party meeting three times on Dec. 3, 2024, after Yoon declared martial law, in an attempt to prevent lawmakers from taking part in a parliamentary vote on ending the emergency decree. Of the 108 PPP lawmakers, 90 were unable to attend the vote to lift the martial law at the time. Special counsel Cho Eun-suk's team had requested a 20-year prison term for Choo. Choo, however, maintained his innocence, saying he had no prior knowledge of the martial law imposition and had received no request from Yoon to block the National Assembly vote. But Kim had never thought of marriage as something he would forgo. “People may be more skeptical about marriage these days, but I’ve never thought I’d stay single,” he said. “I wanted an ordinary life with a spouse and children, and I wanted that sense of stability. To me, an ordinary life is happiness.” With Seoul home prices out of reach, Kim and his partner opted for a jeonse rental, which requires a large upfront deposit. items.summary: Universities must move beyond launching startups and take greater responsibility for helping them survive, grow and deliver lasting benefits to society, global higher education experts said Wednesday. As artificial intelligence (AI) reshapes research and investment, they said, universities should play a more active role in connecting researchers, businesses, investors and governments to turn academic discoveries into real-world solutions. The issue took center stage at a panel discussion titled "Powering innovation ecosystems beyond the playbook: What should universities dare to do next?" at the Times Higher Education (THE) Innovation & Impact Summit 2026. "What matters is how many startups survive, scale and grow, not just how many are created," said Donnie Lygonis, innovation strategist at KTH Innovation, criticizing the tendency to measure universities' entrepreneurial success by the number of startups they launch. Its students spend semesters abroad in cities including Tokyo and New York, then return to Korea in their fourth year for a final project. Wednesday's announcement finalizes a revision to the original plan to merge the three academies into a single institution, as the government sought to offer a compromise amid strong pushback from alumni groups, cadets and other stakeholders. To do so, the Korea Military Academy — the Army college — will move out of Seoul and be relocated to a site in the central-western region of Chungcheong. The appellate bench had convicted Cho after reversing a district court's acquittal. items.summary: Hankuk University of Foreign Studies (HUFS) celebrated the 60th anniversary of its Department of Thai Studies with a series of events, including an international academic conference and a cultural festival, on Nov. 5–6, the university said. Founded in 1966, the department used the anniversary as an opportunity to review its achievements in education and research, explore future directions for Thai studies and discuss ways to expand academic and cultural exchanges between Korea and Thailand. The international conference, titled “Thai Studies Beyond Borders: Transitional Perspectives and Future Directions,” was held on Nov. 5–6 at the library on HUFS’ Seoul campus. Supported by the Korean Association of Thai Studies, HUFS’ Center for Southeast Asian Studies, the university’s Critical Foreign Language Education Program and the Royal Thai Embassy in Seoul, the conference brought together more than 200 scholars from six countries. items.title: Coalition destroys 60 Houthi military targets in Yemen, intercepts cruise missile targeting Riyadh

items.summary: RIYADH — The Coalition to Support Legitimacy in Yemen has destroyed 60 Houthi military targets across four Yemeni governorates and intercepted a cruise missile launched toward Saudi Arabia’s Riyadh region. Coalition spokesperson Maj. Gen. Turki Al-Malki said the targeted operation, announced early Wednesday morning, aimed to weaken the Houthi militia’s ballistic missile and drone capabilities and neutralize maritime threats. Al-Malki said the operation targeted military sites across Sanaa, Al-Hudaydah, Amran and Saada governorates. The operation included the destruction of tunnels used to store ballistic missiles in mountainous areas, along with workshops used to assemble and store drones, according to the Coalition. Later Wednesday morning, the Coalition separately announced that it had intercepted and destroyed a cruise missile launched by the Houthi militia toward Saudi Arabia’s Riyadh region.

items.summary: RIYADH — The Cabinet session, chaired by Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman in Riyadh on Tuesday, reviewed the outcomes of recent talks between Saudi Arabia and friendly nations aimed at broadening the horizons of bilateral and multilateral cooperation across various fields. The Cabinet also underscored the importance of supporting all efforts to reinforce regional security and peace, ensure the stability of energy markets, and safeguard maritime corridors and freedom of navigation, thereby securing the uninterrupted flow of global trade and supply chains. In a statement to the Saudi Press Agency following the session, Minister of Media Salman Al-Dossary said that the Cabinet had been briefed on the overall performance of the state and the progress and achievements made across various fronts, despite the prevailing circumstances and successive transformations unfolding across the world, particularly in the regional environment. The Council affirmed that the Kingdom is moving forward with efforts to further strengthen its capabilities, address emerging developments and challenges, safeguard its development gains and national achievements, and uphold its standing among nations and its influential role at both regional and international levels. The Council of Ministers reviewed the latest developments in the national economy and the resilience it has demonstrated in adapting to diverse circumstances. This resilience is underpinned by the progress made in diversifying sources of economic growth under the framework of Saudi Vision 2030, alongside reforms that have sustained the growth and prosperity of non-oil activities and helped keep inflation at low levels. The review also highlighted continued support for investment, the expansion of opportunities for the private sector, the capacity of public finances to respond to changing conditions, and the sustainability of spending on essential services and development projects. The Cabinet commended the Kingdom’s continued achievements across various international indicators and its advanced global rankings in several fields and criteria related to artificial intelligence, according to the Digital Competitiveness and AI Global Ranking issued by the International Institute for Management Development. These achievements reflect the efforts of the national data system to develop capabilities, stimulate investment, and enhance regulatory frameworks. The Cabinet also regarded the Kingdom’s election to the Council of the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) as an extension of its role in advancing the telecommunications, space, and technology sectors and contributing to the leadership of global digital transformation. It further underscored the Kingdom’s commitment to opening broader horizons for serving humanity, supporting development, and promoting innovation and artificial intelligence. The Cabinet authorized the minister of energy or his deputy to discuss and sign a draft memorandum of understanding (MoU) with the International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA) regarding cooperation in the field of renewable energy between the Saudi ministry of energy and IRENA. It approved a MoU between the Saudi ministry of energy and the ministry of natural resources of Canada for cooperation in the field of energy. The council authorized the chairman of the Board of Directors of the King Abdulaziz Foundation or his deputy to discuss and sign a draft MoU with the Azerbaijani side regarding cooperation in the scientific field between the Foundation and the Institute of Manuscripts of the Azerbaijan National Academy of Sciences, and authorized the minister of Islamic affairs, call and guidance, or his deputy to discuss and sign a draft MoU with the Congolese side regarding cooperation in the field of Islamic affairs between the Saudi ministry of Islamic affairs, call and guidance and the ministry of justice of the Democratic Republic of Congo. The Cabinet authorized the minister of environment, water and agriculture and chairman of the Board of Directors of the Saudi Water Authority or his deputy to discuss and sign with the Singaporean side the draft MoU between the authority and the Singapore National Water Agency in the field of integrated water resources management. The Council approved a MoU between the Saudi Oversight and Anti-Corruption Authority and the Financial Crimes Authority of Mauritius in the field of preventing and combating corruption and related crimes, and two MoUs for cooperation in the field of radio and television broadcasting between the Saudi Broadcasting Authority and the Syrian General Authority for Radio and Television and the National Broadcasting Authority of the Kyrgyz Republic. The Cabinet amended the Code of Law Practice to allow foreign law firms to establish a professional company in the Kingdom, subject to a set of regulations. It also approved implementing the two resolutions of the Supreme Council of the Gulf Cooperation Council at its 41st session held in Al-Ula Governorate, which included approval of the Gulf General Framework for the Public Health Plan for Preparedness and Response in Emergencies, and the Early Health Warning System Guide.

items.title: Public Prosecution Council approves Code of Investigation Procedures
items.title_zh: 检察官委员会批准《调查程序法》
items.summary: RIYADH — The Public Prosecution Council approved the “Code of Investigation and Public Prosecution Procedures,” a guide for Public Prosecution members in carrying out their investigative and prosecutorial duties. The seventh session of the Council was chaired by Attorney General and Council Chairman Dr. Khalid Al-Yousef in Riyadh on Tuesday. The council discussed several agenda items and issued decisions aimed at developing prosecutorial operations and enhancing professional and institutional performance.The code aims to ensure the integrity and legality of procedures, safeguard legal rights and guarantees, and improve the quality of investigative and prosecutorial work. The council also approved the 2027 training plan for Public Prosecution members, reaffirming its commitment to continuous professional development and strengthening legal capabilities and specialized skills.On personnel matters, the council approved the promotion of 179 Public Prosecution members and adopted several other administrative decisions in accordance with applicable laws and regulations. The decisions form part of the council’s ongoing efforts to develop the prosecutorial system, strengthen professional qualifications, and invest in human capital to improve institutional performance and ensure high standards in prosecutorial practice.

items.title: Coalition intercepts Houthi drone in Riyadh region
items.title_zh: 联军在利雅得地区拦截胡塞武装无人机
items.summary: RIYADH — The Coalition to Restore Legitimacy in Yemen intercepted and destroyed a drone, launched by the terrorist Houthi militia, in the Riyadh region. This was disclosed by Maj. Gen. Turki Al-Maliki, spokesperson of the Coalition.

items.title: Arabian gazelle’s desert adaptability reflected in Arab heritage
items.title_zh: 阿拉伯瞪羚的沙漠适应性反映在阿拉伯文化遗产中
items.summary: RAFHA — Ancient Arabic writings recorded observations of gazelles’ ability to endure thirst and adapt to desert environments. One traditional description portrays the gazelle as compensating for the absence of water by breathing in the breeze, an expression that reflects early Arab observations of the animal’s nature and its ability to survive in arid habitats.Chairman of the Board of Aman Environmental Association in Northern Borders Region Nasser Al-Mujlad said traditional descriptions of the gazelle went beyond its agility and speed to explore its feeding habits, how it copes with water scarcity, and the ways it responds to potential threats, the Saudi Press Agency reported. He explained that gazelles benefit from the moisture in the plants they feed on, including desert grasses and shrubs, helping them withstand dry conditions and reduce their reliance on surface water sources. **media[2795979]**Scientific data published by the Royal Commission for AlUla indicate that the Arabian gazelle (Gazella arabica) can meet its water requirements through its plant-based diet, without necessarily needing to drink water directly. Its diet includes plant leaves, flowers and fruits, including those of acacia trees. **media[2795980]**Al-Mujlad noted that gazelles’ ability to adapt to desert conditions is linked to their diet and grazing behavior, as well as physiological characteristics that help them withstand arid environments. These traits offer a glimpse into the gazelle’s natural adaptation to its surroundings, while traditional accounts reflect the keen interest of ancient Arabs in observing desert wildlife and documenting its behavior.

items.title: Saudi Arabia records 1.8 million electronic car rental contracts in Q3 2026
items.title_zh: 2026年第三季度，沙特阿拉伯的电子汽车租赁合同数量达到180万份
items.summary: RIYADH — Car rental companies in Saudi Arabia issued more than 1.8 million unified electronic contracts during the third quarter of 2026, according to data released by the Transport General Authority. The figure highlights the scale of activity in the sector and the growing reliance on digital solutions to streamline rental transactions.According to the data, the Riyadh region accounted for the largest share of electronic contracts issued across the Kingdom, reaching 30 percent, followed by the Makkah region with 24 percent, the Eastern Province with 14 percent, and Asir with 8 percent.Madinah ranked next with a 6 percent share, followed by Qassim 5 percent, Jazan 4 percent, and Tabuk 3 percent. The remaining 6 percent was distributed among the Kingdom’s other regions. The authority explained that the unified electronic contract helps safeguard the rights of both lessors and lessees, enhance transaction reliability, improve service quality, streamline rental procedures, and boost the efficiency of operational processes.The authority continues to pursue initiatives to develop the car rental sector by enhancing service quality and improving operational efficiency, thereby supporting the sector’s growth and long-term sustainability.

items.title: HR Ministry: No agreement with Kenya for recruitment of skilled workers
items.title_zh: 人力资源部：未与肯尼亚就招聘技术工人达成协议
items.summary: RIYADH — The Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development has confirmed that the technical annex signed with Kenya is exclusively intended to regulate the recruitment of domestic workers and does not cover the recruitment of skilled workers for various sectors. The ministry clarified that no agreement is currently in place for the recruitment of skilled workers from Kenya.In a clarifying statement issued on Tuesday, the ministry explained that the recruitment of domestic workers from Kenya is confined to specific occupations, including domestic workers and private drivers, and does not extend to employment opportunities in other professional sectors.Last Thursday, Deputy Minister of Human Resources and Social Development for Labor Abdullah Abuthnain and Kenya’s Cabinet Secretary for Labour and Social Protection Alfred Nganga Mutua signed a technical annex to the agreement on the recruitment of domestic workers between Saudi Arabia and Kenya that had signed on July 5, 2026. The signing ceremony was held during the visit of Alfred Nganga Mutua to Riyadh. The annex is part of efforts to strengthen cooperation and develop the technical and regulatory mechanisms governing the recruitment of domestic workers.The ministry noted that the technical annex is built around three key pillars: reducing recruitment costs, enhancing the quality of domestic workers through training and qualification programs, and safeguarding the rights of all parties involved in the contractual relationship.For its part, the Kenyan side expressed its readiness to supply domestic workers in accordance with the regulations and procedures in force in the Kingdom, while adhering to the stipulated recruitment costs and timeframes. Recruitment will be based on actual demand and the requirements of employers, both citizens and residents.The ministry underscored the importance of ensuring accuracy when disseminating recruitment-related information, urging the public to rely exclusively on its official sources, including its website and social media accounts.

items.title: Saudi Arabia strongly condemns repeated Iranian attacks on Bahrain
items.title_zh: 沙特阿拉伯强烈谴责伊朗屡次袭击巴林
items.summary: RIYADH — The Ministry of Foreign Affairs expressed Saudi Arabia’s strongest condemnation of the repeated Iranian attacks on Bahrain, describing them as a flagrant violation of international law and the principles of good neighborliness. “These attacks undermine peace efforts and ongoing endeavors to safeguard the security and stability of the region and its people,” the ministry said in a statement.Saudi Arabia reaffirmed its full solidarity with Bahrain in all measures it takes to safeguard its security and stability. The Kingdom also stressed the urgent need for an immediate halt to all blatant Iranian attacks against the countries of the region, while underscoring the importance of allowing diplomatic efforts to pursue peace and resolve the crisis through negotiations, the statement added.

items.title: King Salman Royal Reserve records two births of vulnerable Arabian gazelles
items.title_zh: 萨勒曼国王皇家保护区记录了两只濒危阿拉伯瞪羚的出生
items.summary: SKAKA — The King Salman bin Abdulaziz Royal Reserve recorded two new Arabian gazelle births in November 2026, as part of its ongoing efforts to reintroduce wildlife species, enhance biodiversity and restore ecological balance within the reserve. The Arabian gazelle (Gazella arabica), locally known as “Al-Idmi,” is classified as Vulnerable on the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) Red List and is among the species targeted by the reserve’s reintroduction programs. **media[2795757]** Female Arabian gazelles typically give birth to one offspring at a time, making the two recorded births particularly significant for conservation efforts aimed at protecting the species. The reserve previously recorded Arabian gazelle births in 2024. The latest births indicate the success of the reserve’s care and breeding programs, as well as the suitability of its natural habitats for supporting the species and sustaining its reproduction. **media[2795759]** The King Salman bin Abdulaziz Royal Reserve Development Authority continues to implement initiatives aimed at protecting wildlife, developing natural habitats and reintroducing native species into their original environments. These efforts contribute to restoring ecological balance, enriching biodiversity and advancing Saudi Arabia’s environmental sustainability objectives.

items.title: Market value of Saudi Exchange’s intangible assets surges to SR5.78 trillion
items.title_zh: 沙特交易所无形资产的市场价值飙升至5.78万亿里亚尔
items.summary: RIYADH — The market value of intangible assets held by companies listed on the Saudi Exchange reached approximately SR5.78 trillion at the end of 2025, accounting for 65.6 percent of their total market value, according to Intangible Assets 2025 in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia report issued by the Saudi Authority for Intellectual Property (SAIP).The value of intangible assets disclosed in financial statements stood at approximately SR311.52 billion, the report pointed out. The report examines the current state of intangible assets, their economic value, and their role in enhancing competitiveness and supporting knowledge- and innovation-based economic growth, in line with the objectives of Saudi Vision 2030. It aims to measure the market value of intangible assets held by companies listed on the Saudi Exchange and analyze their distribution across sectors. The report’s publication is part of SAIP’s efforts to raise awareness of the economic value of intangible assets and support the development of practices for managing and investing in them, thereby contributing to stimulating innovation, attracting investment, and enhancing the competitiveness of the national economy.
